Can you provide a single PDF with the annotated diagram and a small spreadsheet that maps artifacts to controls? Ideally we'd have this by COB PT today as Graystone is on a tight review schedule.

Thanks Hannah — sending my annotated pass. Key notes baked into diagram callouts and short rationale below. Attaching: redwood_chokepoint_topology_v1_annotated.pdf.

Summary callouts (short):
- Management Plane API (control.redwood.internal): only reachable from our control plane fabric; not routable from customer VPCs. Hardened by mTLS mutual auth, ingress restricted to management subnets and operator bastion IPs, logged to audit pipeline. Evidence: mTLS cert rotation logs and ingress ACL snippets.

- Ingress Reverse Proxy (edge-proxy-infer): handles tenant requests for hosted only. For Dedicated/Private we run an internal proxy instance per-tenant pool; these proxies accept traffic from customer peering only when explicitly configured. Evidence: per-tenant proxy config (redacted) and peering ACL checklist.

- KV-cache/Model-serving control channel: internal gRPC channel over private fabric. Customer VPCs do not have access. Fallback path during AZ outage relies on brokered routing inside our backbone — no external exposure. Evidence: routing policy extract and failover playbook.

- Operator bastion / SRE management jump: accessible via customer-managed SSO-controlled jumpbox (SAML), with just-in-time access via our PAM. Evidence: PAM audit excerpt and SSO session logs (redacted).

I also added a "chokepoint severity" tag (low/med/high) per item for reviewer context.
